description: Single-panel line plot of compressive yield stress versus test temperature for five Fe–15Al-based alloys. The x-axis is labelled "Temperature [°C]" and runs 0–900 with gridlines every 100; the y-axis is labelled "Yield stress in compression [MPa]" and runs 0–900 with gridlines every 100. An inset legend in the upper-right gives the marker key: Fe–15Al (plus), Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C (cross), Fe–15Al–2V–1C (open circle), Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C (open triangle) and Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C (open square). At the lowest temperature the two Nb/Ta-containing alloys lie highest, between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines, far above Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C (near the 500 MPa gridline), Fe–15Al–2V–1C (slightly below the 400 MPa gridline) and binary Fe–15Al (between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines). All five curves fall monotonically as temperature increases; the Nb- and Ta-bearing curves collapse steeply between ~600 and 800 °C, and by 800 °C all curves converge low, between the 0 and 100 MPa gridlines. The figure demonstrates that Ta or Nb additions raise the compressive yield strength of Fe–15Al at every tested temperature, with no anomalous strength peak.

observations.observation: The figure is a line plot of yield stress in compression [MPa] (y-axis, 0–900) against Temperature [°C] (x-axis, 0–900) with five separate curves.
The inset legend identifies the curves as Fe–15Al (plus), Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C (cross), Fe–15Al–2V–1C (open circle), Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C (open triangle) and Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C (open square).
Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C and Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C show the highest yield stress at all plotted temperatures; both start between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines at the lowest temperature.
Binary Fe–15Al (plus markers) shows the lowest yield stress over the whole temperature range, starting between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines.
Fe–15Al–2Ti–1C starts near the 500 MPa gridline at low temperature, above Fe–15Al–2V–1C and binary Fe–15Al but well below the Nb- and Ta-containing alloys.
All five curves decrease monotonically with increasing temperature; no anomalous peak in yield stress is visible in this figure.
The Nb- and Ta-containing curves fall steeply between roughly 600 °C and 700 °C, and by 800 °C all five curves have converged to low values between the 0 and 100 MPa gridlines.
No numeric data labels or error bars are printed on the plot; the yield-stress values are readable only relative to the 100 MPa gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows the temperature dependency of the yield stress in compression for Fe–15Al-based alloys.
The citing text states the yield stresses of all Fe–15Al-based alloys show a gradual monotonous decrease with increasing temperature.
The citing text states that the alloys with Nb or Ta show the highest strength at all tested temperatures, which agrees with the curve ordering in the plot.
The citing text states the alloys were tested at elevated temperatures up to 800 °C, consistent with the plotted x-axis range.
The citing text attributes an anomalous yield-strength peak at intermediate temperature to the Fe–26Al-based alloys shown in Fig. 6, not to this Fe–15Al figure.

unreadable_items: No numeric values are printed on the curves or axes beyond the 100-unit gridline ticks; individual data-point coordinates cannot be read exactly from the image.
